1.why: Reset verify requires record.sessionId === session.id, so the token must belong to the requesting session/user.

2.why: A token bound to another session fails the sessionId check and cannot be used by a different user/session.

3.why: Password change only clears mfaVerified on the current session and never deletes or invalidates other entries in the sessions map.

4.why: HTTPS is served with TLS certs and HTTP 308-redirects to HTTPS with HSTS, though the exact TLS version is not pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 verifiers and passwords with argon2id; MFA codes themselves remain plaintext in memory.

6.why: No email is sent at all; the API returns testingToken/testingMfaCode in JSON instead of a guarded email message.

7.why: Contact, token, and password inputs are strictly validated; the UI writes untrusted data with textContent only.

8.why: Client navigation uses same-origin paths only and the HTTP server redirects solely to this host’s HTTPS URL.

9.why: There are no email templates that embed user input or scripts.

10.why: Recovery/MFA testing tokens are returned in API JSON and appended to the on-page Logs panel.

11.why: Password hash comes from env/argon2id, but MFA secret codes are hardcoded literals in the source.

12.why: No default password exists; login requires a non-empty INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH and Bun.password.verify.

13.why: recordAttempt/blocked enforce per-action limits (e.g. 3–5 tries) with a 60s lockout.

14.why: Recovery always returns the same generic eligibility message regardless of whether the contact is valid.

15.why: Reset tokens are randomHex(32) (64-char hex), single-use, expiry-bound, and tied to the requester’s session.
